input:
We are bringing up LPDDR6 (JEDEC JESD209-6, July 2025) on a next-gen flagship SoC, running at 14400 MT/s. During PHY training the bootloader logs:

  [boot] LPDDR6 PHY training failed at 14.4 GT/s; fallback to 12.0 GT/s

The fallback succeeds but we lose 20% memory bandwidth, which hurts AI inference throughput. VDD2H is 1.00V and VDD2L is 0.95V per JEDEC. What are the likely root-cause categories? Which JEDEC-mandated supplies and per-sub-channel signals should we verify? How does LPDDR6's 4×24-bit sub-channel topology constrain PCB trace-length matching vs LPDDR5X?
